description: Dive deep into the archival collections of IU Libraries through a screening series of rare and unique archival films that center traditionally underrepresented narratives and underrepresented motion-picture practices, pushing on and expanding the spectrum of what is considered "cinema."  In an effort to keep audiences open-minded and with limited pre-conceptions of these rare works of celluloid, descriptions of films to be shown will not be shared prior to screenings. Trust us, you (probably) haven't seen these films before!December Program: Best Practices: Films for Safe Living curated by Dave RodriguezProgram Description: Can a film save your life? Can it give you a design for living? These will certainly try.Curator Bio: Dave Rodriguez is a media artist, musician, and curator from Miami, FL, currently based in Bloomington, IN. His film and video work has screened in festivals and galleries across the Americas and Europe including the Ann Arbor Film Festival, the Chicago Underground Film Festival, Mono No Aware, Third Horizon, and others. He has over 15 years of professional experience working in film labs, libraries, archives, and museum collections, publishing in places like Found Footage Magazine, the Journal of Academic Librarianship, and most recently in the Review of Japanese Culture and Society. In Bloomington he spends his time taking care of many plants, one old cat, and supporting local organizations like Cicada Cinema and the Bloomington Synth Community.Please register below! title: Sarah Jarosz: 10 Years of Undercurrent
location: Buskirk-Chumley Theater,114 East Kirkwood Avenue, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Originally from Wimberley, Texas, Sarah Jarosz is a six-time GRAMMY Award winning singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. Since her recorded debut in 2009, she has released seven solo albums and two albums with I’m With Her, her band with Sara Watkins and Aoife O’Donovan.

In addition to her multiple GRAMMY, Americana Music Association, and Folk Alliance awards, her work has received widespread critical praise from publications including Rolling Stone, The New York Times, and USA Today. Jarosz has appeared three times on PBS’s legendary Austin City Limits television show and numerous times on A Prairie Home Companion, Live From Here, and the Grand Ole Opry. She is currently based in Nashville, Tennessee.

Jordan Tice is an award-winning guitarist and songwriter described by the Fretboard Journal as “quite simply, one of our favorite acoustic guitarists performing today.” He has 7 projects to his name as a solo artist and 6 as a founding member of the string band, Hawktail.

Equally virtuosic as a flatpicker and fingerstylist, and with a casual vocal style, Tice conjures ingredients from far-flung worlds with ease. His performances call upon the repertories of American and British Isles folk, bluegrass, blues and pop-oriented songs, and though his earlier releases are instrumental in focus, he has been carefully honing his craft as a singer-songwriter in his most recent work. This includes his albums Motivational Speakeasy (produced by Kenneth Pattengale of The Milk Carton Kids and praised by NPR Music as “a really wonderful record”), Wild Rose of Morning (a collaboration with Andrew Marlin and Christian Sedelmyer), and Badlettsville.

He has performed at festivals such as the Grey Fox Bluegrass Festival, Green Mountain Bluegrass and Roots, Red Wing Roots, Wintergrass Music Festival, and the Strawberry Music Festival and opened for artists like Watchhouse, I’m With Her, The Milk Carton Kids, and Madison Cunningham. In addition to his solo and collaborative work, he has performed and recorded as a sideman with Americana artists such as David Rawlings, Yola, Andrew Marlin and Aoife O’Donovan.

title: New Music Ensemble – David Dzubay, director; Dai Fujikura, guest composer; Sara Erb, alumna guest bassoon
description: Repertoire  Augusta Read Thomas: Solstice Ritual (2024)Donald Erb: The Towers of Silence (1974)Dai Fujikura: Bassoon Concerto No. 2 (2026)About the DirectorDavid Dzubay's compositions have been performed in the United States, Europe, Canada, Mexico, and Asia by the symphony orchestras of Aspen, Atlanta, Baltimore, Boston, Cincinnati, Detroit, Fort Wayne, Guangxi, Guiyang, Honolulu, Kansas City, Louisville, Memphis, Minnesota, Oregon, Oakland, St. Louis and Vancouver; the American Composers Orchestra, National Symphonies of Ireland and Mexico, New World Symphony, National Repertory Orchestra, and New York Youth Symphony; and ensembles including the Grossman Ensemble, Le Nouvel Ensemble Moderne, Onix, Manhattan and St. Louis Brass Quintets, Voices of Change, the Alexander, Orion and Pacifica string quartets, the League/ISCM, Earplay, and the San Francisco Contemporary Music Players. His music has been championed by conductors including James DePreist, George Hanson, Keith Lockhart, David Loebel, Michael Morgan, Eiji Oue, Richard Pittman, Iván del Prado, Mark Russell Smith, Lawrence Leighton Smith, Michael Stern, Carl Topilow, David Wiley, Kirk Trevor, Thomas Wilkins, and David Zinman. Honors include two Fromm Music Foundation commissions; Guggenheim, MacDowell, Yaddo, Copland House, and Djerassi fellowships; the Kuhmo Chamber Music Festival Composition Competition, Indianapolis Chamber Orchestra Composition Competition, Utah Arts Festival Commission, William Revelli and Walter Beeler Memorial Prizes, Wayne Peterson Prize; and grants from the Aaron Copland Fund for Music for two portrait CDs. Currently professor of music and director of the New Music Ensemble at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music in Bloomington, Dzubay was previously on the faculty of the University of North Texas in Denton. Since 2011, he has taught composition for three weeks each summer at the Brevard Music Center. From 1995 to 1998, he served as composer-consultant to the Minnesota Orchestra and during the 2005-06 season, he was Meet the Composer/American Symphony Orchestra League Music Alive Composer-in-Residence with the Green Bay Symphony Orchestra. Dzubay has conducted at the Tanglewood, Aspen, and June in Buffalo festivals as well as the National Symphony of Columbia, Grossman Ensemble, League of Composers Orchestra, Pittsburgh New Music Ensemble, Music from China, and Voices of Change.Five Friends Master Class Series – Honoring Robert SamelsThe Five Friends Master Class Series honoring the lives of five talented Jacobs School of Music students—Chris Carducci, Garth Eppley, Georgina Joshi, Zachary Novak, and Robert Samels—was established in 2012 with a gift of $1 million from the Georgina Joshi Foundation, Inc. This annual series of lectures, master classes, and residencies by a number of the world's leading musicians and teachers focuses on areas of interest most relevant to the lives of the five friends—voice performance, choral conducting, early music, music theory, composition, and opera. The Georgina Joshi Foundation was established in 2007 as the vision of Georgina Joshi's mother, Louise Addicott-Joshi, to provide educational and career development opportunities for young musicians and to encourage and support public performance of music. The gift to the school establishes a permanent way for the world to learn about each of the five friends, their musical talents and passions, and to encourage the development of similar talents and passions in current and future music students. The establishment of this endowment by the families is administered by the IU Foundation.  Bass-baritone and composer Robert Samels was born on June 2, 1981, and died in a plane crash on April 20, 2006. He was a doctoral student in choral conducting at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music and had studied voice with Giorgio Tozzi and Costanza Cuccaro. He began his vocal studies with Alfred Anderson at the University of Akron and Andreas Poulimenos at Bowling Green State University. Samels had recently appeared as Mr. Gibbs in the world premiere of Our Town by Ned Rorem, as Marco in the collegiate premiere of William Bolcom's A View from the Bridge, and as Joseph and Herod in the collegiate premiere of El Nino by John Adams. In September 2005, he conducted the premiere of his own opera, Pilatvs. As a member of the Wolf Trap Opera Company for 2006, he would have added three roles that summer, including Bartolo in Le Nozze di Figaro, Friar Laurence in Roméo et Juliette, and Pluto in Telemann's Orpheus. Other opera credits included the title roles of Don Pasquale and Il Turco in Italia, as well as Leporello in Don Giovanni, Falstaff in TheMerry Wives of Windsor, and Bottom in A Midsummer Night's Dream. In the summer of 2004, he performed Creon in the New York premiere of John Eaton's Antigone. Samels also frequently performed in the oratorio repertoire. In the spring of 2005, he was selected as a semi-finalist in the annual competition of the Oratorio Society of New York. He was an announcer with public radio station WFIU, as well as the host and producer of its Cantabile program. A soloist with Aguavá New Music Studio, he had recently performed a concert at the Library of Congress. Samels was an associate instructor in the Jacobs School's Music Theory Department, where was loved and admired by his students.

title: Denny Love: Show Love Tour
location: The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN
description: Introducing Denny Love, a Los Angeles–based actor and comedian whose career seamlessly bridges prestige television, live comedy, and viral digital culture. A celebrated alumnus of DePaul University’s renowned Theatre School, Denny first broke through with a standout performance in Hulu’s Looking for Alaska, a critically acclaimed series boasting a 92% Rotten Tomatoes rating. He went on to appear in two seasons of Taylor Sheridan’s hit Paramount+ drama Mayor of Kingstown, further solidifying his dramatic range. Beyond the screen, Denny is a commanding live performer who has shared stages with comedy heavyweights like Chris D’Elia and delivered memorable sets opening for Theo Von. As a key cast member of @KevinLangue’s viral YouTube and TikTok content, he has helped build a digital powerhouse of over 4.47 million subscribers and more than 2 billion views worldwide. Denny Love’s live stand up presence is rapidly becoming one of the most exciting forces in comedy. He’s been taking the comedy scene by storm by performing at the most coveted venues in and around the LA area, across the country and internationally. Most notably; The Laugh Factory, The Comedy Store, Improv, Haha Comedy Club, Comedy Chateau, Jam in the Van, Don’t Tell Comedy, Can’t Even, and many more. He recently headlined at the Tokyo Comedy Bar in Tokyo, Japan and ROR Comedy Club in Osaka, Japan. Denny was seen on stages all across America and Canada while on tour with Chris D’elia and most recently in Las Vegas with Theo Von. In 2026, he takes the stage at Netflix Is a Joke, solidifying his place among the most sought-after rising voices in entertainment. This summer, he joins the Kevin Langue Show as a key performer on an ambitious 18- city national theatre tour, bringing his sharp timing and undeniable charisma to audiences across the country. Building on that momentum, Denny will launch his first headlining tour in Fall 2026, marking a major milestone as he steps fully into his own spotlight.

title: It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop
description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.  


It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.  


Instructions:  


Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session 


If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop. 


If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu. 


All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all IU students and other members of the Indiana University community. 


Hosted by: Office for Sexual Violence Prevention and Victim Advocacy

title: First Mondays Wellness Workshops
description:
Feeling well is an ongoing journey - join us on the first Monday of every month to work on your wellness!
Our workshops are engaging and interactive - no lectures here. You will learn new skills and have a chance to share your concerns, if you choose. We are here to help you develop skills that will take you from IU into the future.
September: Stress Management
Build your stress management strengths! Understand more about how stress can impact your life and what you can do to take control.
October: Time Management
Life doesn't have to be a crush - learn how to manage your time and get some back for yourself
November: Supporting Each Other
How can we help each other as we navigate challenges? Learn how to identify when a friend might need help and steps to take to start the conversation.
December: Mindfulness and Meditation
Learn five-minute meditations, and try out relaxation stations to learn skills to build your chill.

title: It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop
description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.  


It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.  


Instructions:  


Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session 


If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop. 


If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu.

title: Scholarly Write-In
description:
Write and work in solidarity with other IU scholars. We offer a silent work environment with coffee and natural light. The write-in is open to all graduate students (at any stage of their degree program).

 

We will check in at the beginning of our meeting, set some goals together, then work independently for a few hours. Fifteen minutes prior to the close of the meeting, we will reconvene to update each other on our progress and set broad goals for the coming week.

This is a casual meeting – feel free to come for as much or as little time as you like, and only during the weeks that work for you. You are welcome and encouraged to work on anything that you need time and space for: participants regularly work on dissertations, course papers, syllabi and lesson plans, articles and pieces for publication, and grading. Our goal is to create a space where we can work together in solidarity on whatever projects we need to each week.

Meets weekly throughout the semester, Thursday from 1-3pm. No meeting during Thanksgiving break.

Co-sponsored by Writing Tutorial Services and the IU Libraries.

title: Annie
location: Waldron Arts Center,122 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Annie” on stage December 10th - January 3rd at the Waldron Auditorium.

Discover the magic of Annie, the iconic Broadway musical that has captured hearts for generations! The timeless tale of Little Orphan Annie follows a tenacious young girl whose unbreakable optimism leads her on an unforgettable journey from a New York City orphanage to a place she can finally call home. Featuring one of Broadway’s most memorable scores, including “It’s the Hard-Knock Life,” “Easy Street,” “N.Y.C.” and the endlessly-uplifting “Tomorrow,” Annie is a delightful theatrical experience for the entire family. Fun for all ages!

See Constellation’s website for more information, including a detailed performance schedule. Learn more and find tickets at seeconstellation.org/kids/annie/ https://seeconstellation.org/kids/annie/

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road parking lot. The gate is open. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you like to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the parking lot at the base of Gose Creek Road at the end of Hinson Road in Martinsville.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: Cirque Éloize
description: Making its IU Auditorium debut, Cirque Éloize has been a creative force and ambassador for Quebec culture for over three decades. As a precursor to contemporary circus, the company constantly reinvents the art of encounter by combining circus, music, dance, theater, and technology to offer experiences that go beyond simple entertainment and remain etched in the minds of audiences.     In Bloomington, they'll perform an evening-length work titled iD – Evolution. Acrobats defy gravity, dancers explode into striking urban movements, and every space is transformed into a playground for the imagination. Trampoline, aerial hoop, trial bike, breakdancing, and many other disciplines intertwine in an electrifying performance where every jump, every movement, and every note of music tells a story.   iD – Evolution explores identity and encounter in a world where bodies speak, clash, and respond to each other. It is an experience that shakes the senses, transports, and amazes—a visual and auditory journey where poetry and urban energy merge to create a show that is both spectacular and deeply human.

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you like to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the parking lot at the base of Gose Creek Road at the end of Hinson Road in Martinsville.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: Global Competencies Skills Development Series: White House Situation Room to Big Tech - Career Dinner w/ Belinda Jackson Farrier & Shelby Smith-Wilson
description: Cold messages on LinkedIn rarely lead to meaningful career breakthroughs. This session gives you direct, unscripted access to two senior executives whose careers bridge the highest levels of international diplomacy, national security, and Silicon Valley leadership.  Feel free to drop in as your schedule allows and stay for as long as your evening permits. You do not need to attend the full duration to participate, grab dinner, and engage with our guests.  Who You Will Meet  You will connect directly with two former Senior Foreign Service officers and global executive leaders:A Former Director for Global Rapid Response at Google (YouTube Trust & Safety): A career diplomat who served in the White House Situation Room and the State Department Operations Center before transitioning to top tier tech leadership.    A Senior Government Executive & Diplomat across 5 Countries: An expert in crisis management, strategic negotiations, and executive leadership who prepares senior officials for high stakes global environments.      Together, they also co-host the Leadership Tea Podcast and run their own executive advisory firms.  Value for Every Degree LevelUndergraduate Students: Learn how to break into competitive sectors like foreign policy, national security, and tech strategy directly from women who held those roles.    Master Students: Get realistic strategies for translating government and public policy tradecraft into high value roles in corporate policy, tech, and consulting.    PhD Candidates: Learn how to compress complex academic research into punchy executive briefs that cabinet secretaries and C-suite leaders actually read.      Key Discussion TopicsWriting Under Pressure: Mastering Bottom Line Up Front frameworks for high level decision makers.    The Government to Tech Pivot: Moving from government operations to senior roles in Silicon Valley.    Crisis Leadership: Managing teams and making critical decisions when information is limited and stakes are high.      Speaker ProfilesBelinda Jackson Farrier  Belinda Jackson Farrier is the Founder of Sweetgrass Advisory Group and co-host of the Leadership Tea Podcast. She served as a career member of the Senior Foreign Service with the U.S. Department of State, holding postings in Rwanda, El Salvador, Togo, and Peru. In Washington, her assignments included the State Department Operations Center, the White House Situation Room, and the Washington Foreign Press Center. She later joined Google, where she served as Director for Global Rapid Response in YouTube Trust and Safety.Shelby Smith-Wilson  Shelby Smith-Wilson is the Founder of The FendAll Collaborative and co-host of the Leadership Tea Podcast. A senior government executive, diplomat, and leadership strategist, her global career spans five countries. She specializes in change and crisis management, strategic negotiation, and cross-cultural leadership, advising senior executives on guiding organizations through complex structural transitions and high stakes disruptions.

title: Shucked
description: The Tony Award-winning musical comedy Shucked makes its IU Auditorium debut in 2027.     Maizy and Beau are getting hitched, when the corn that protects their small community starts to die. The town needs answers. But who will dare venture beyond the borders of Cob County?     Including the knockout songs "Woman of the World," "Somebody Will," and "Independently Owned," this Broadway hit about an unlikely hero, an unscrupulous con artist, and a battle for the heart and soil of a small town, is not to be missed.

title: No School - FLEX Day #2 - Teachers Only
Global Competencies Skills Development Series: Writing Under Pressure: A Diplomatic & Digital Crisis Simulation
description: Never Done a Simulation Before? You Belong Here.  You do not need to be a political science expert, a tech guru, or a public speaker to attend. If you have never done a simulation before, this is designed specifically for you to try something brand new in a zero-pressure environment.  Got 20 or 30 minutes between classes? Drop in whenever your morning permits, grab free snacks and drinks, and jump right in.  What Actually Happens in the Room?  Imagine breaking news hits: foreign civil unrest erupts, viral AI fakes flood social media, and leaked messages throw everything into chaos. Top decision-makers at the White House or Google do not have time for a 10-page essay—they need a 4-sentence update right now. Working alongside a small team, you will dive into a fast-moving, live-edited scenario where you separate signal from noise, filter out fake information, and learn how to draft high-stakes executive briefs in real time with guidance from seasoned experts.  Why Show Up?Master the BLUF Method: Learn the "Bottom Line Up Front" writing trick that top diplomats, intelligence analysts, and Silicon Valley managers use to write emails decision-makers actually read.    The "Cut 30%" Challenge: Learn how to edit out fluff and sound clear and confident in your everyday writing.    Low Friction: Drop in, grab food, work with a small group, and leave when you need to head to your next class. No prep work or prior reading required.      Target Audience  Open to ALL undergraduate, Master, and PhD students across HLS, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Public Policy, Informatics, and related majors. Staff and faculty are welcome too!

title: Global Competencies Skills Development Series: Disaster Response, Humanitarian Systems & Crisis Leadership Dinner
description: Directing Responses in the World's Complex Crises  When natural disasters, complex emergencies, or global health crises strike, how do international humanitarian systems deploy aid, manage logistics, and make high-stakes choices on the ground?  Join the Global Competencies Skills Development Series for an intimate, off-the-record conversation with Michael Jack—former USAID Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance Division Director, international disaster management strategist, and certified leadership coach.  Michael has served on the front lines of major U.S. government international disaster responses, including the Iraq Sinjar crisis, West Africa Ebola outbreak, Mexico City earthquake, South Sudan complex emergency, Amazon wildfires, and the Northern Ethiopia response.  Skip high-level theory. This session breaks down raw operational tradecraft: leading cross-agency disaster systems, managing risk under extreme uncertainty, and building the personal stamina required for high-stakes international careers.

title: Legally Blonde – The Musical
description: OMG, you guys!!! Legally Blonde – The Musical is coming to Bloomington!     Fabulously fun and international award-winning Legally Blonde is the ultimate Broadway tribute to girl power! The story follows the transformation of Elle Woods  as she tackles stereotypes, sexism, snobbery, and scandal in pursuit of her dreams and proves that you can be both legally blonde AND the smartest person in the room. This contemporary, topical story touches on many current hot button issues while delighting audiences with memorable songs and explosive dances. Legally Blonde warms the heart by proving that self-discovery never goes out of style!     Elle Woods appears to have it all. Her life is turned upside down, however, when her boyfriend dumps her so he can start getting more serious about his life and attend Harvard Law. Determined to get him back, Elle uses her brain and ingenuity to get into Harvard too. School begins with endless struggles, but with the help of her new friends, Elle quickly realizes her potential and her true assets, as she sets out to prove herself to the world and make everyone a believer.     Based on the iconic movie starring Reese Witherspoon, Legally Blonde will take you from the sorority house to the halls of justice with Broadway's brightest heroine and, of course, her Chihuahua, Bruiser.

description:

When Sylvia decides to expose her latest affair to her husband—and her lover’s wife—an idyllic English countryside getaway turns into a wildly improper disaster. As lovers and spouses collide under one roof, what begins as a scandal quickly spirals into a cascade of outrageous twists, romantic entanglements, and deliciously bad decisions. From the writer of the smash-hit stage adaptation of Clue, The Cottage is a fast-paced farce that delivers big laughs, bold antics, and a giant dose of high-society mischief.
